euronews.description: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko told the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk that, despite recent diplomatic tensions between the two countries, the atmosphere at the gathering was friendly, and that Ukraine should look to Poland as a model for infrastructure development and modernisation.

rfi.title: Punishing heatwave exposes cracks in France's nuclear power fleet
rfi.description: Three French nuclear plants halted production during this week's record-breaking heatwave as rivers became too warm to cool them, raising questions over the long-term future of Europe's biggest nuclear fleet.

rfi.title: Israel's targeting of Gaza's children proves genocidal intent, UN inquiry finds
rfi.description: The deliberate targeting of Palestinian children is central to a United Nations-mandated report's conclusion that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. The commission argues that children have not only been victims of the war, but have been targeted in ways that help establish genocidal intent. Israel has dismissed the findings of the report, released this week, as "defamatory".

rfi.title: France heatwave overwhelms hospitals and forces Pride march delay
rfi.description: Emergency doctors at one of Paris's biggest hospitals warned on Friday that wards had become dangerously overcrowded after a week of soaring temperatures, as authorities restricted public alcohol consumption, organisers postponed the annual Pride march and €130 million was pledged to help schools adapt to climate change.

rfi.title: Current Europe heatwave 'impossible' without human-induced climate change
rfi.description: A study comparing the heatwave that has swept across Europe this week with heatwaves in 1976 and 2003 has found that human-caused climate change is "unequivocally" responsible for the extreme heat over the last week – with France recording its hottest day since records began in 1947 on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Calls for child protection reforms in wake of schoolgirl Lyhanna's death
rfi.description: An investigation into previous child rape allegations against the suspect in the death of a schoolgirl in southern France has revealed failures by prosecutors and police. The case has unleashed a wave of criticism over how sexual and gender-based violence cases are handled in France, with victims, families and advocates pushing for reform.

rfi.title: Historic heatwave catches Europe's fashion industry unprepared
rfi.description: The most coveted accessory at the Paris Fashion Week shows this week was not a bag, a sneaker or a watch. It was an ice pack.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’

rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

lemonde.description: Depuis trois jours, les passages aux urgences du centre hospitalier régional Metz-Thionville ont augmenté de 20 % et les appels vers le centre de régulation de 40 %.

lemonde.description: Kylian Mbappé et ses coéquipiers ont largement dominé, vendredi, les Lions norvégiens (4-1), qui se sont privés d’Erling Haaland. Les Bleus disputeront leur seizième de finale de la Coupe du monde, mardi à 23 heures.

lemonde.title: Israël et le Liban signent un accord-cadre avec les Etats-Unis, une « première étape » vers la paix, affirme Marco Rubio
lemonde.description: Les trois parties n’ont pas dévoilé le contenu de l’accord. Le premier ministre israélien, Benyamin Nétanyahou, a répété que l’armée de l’Etat hébreu resterait dans le sud du Liban jusqu’à ce que le Hezbollah rende les armes.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan s’alourdit à 920 morts, plus de 50 000 personnes portées disparues
lemonde.description: Les agences de l’ONU et d’autres organisations humanitaires ont réclamé un « accès humanitaire rapide et sans entrave », rappelant que des millions de personnes faisaient face à une insécurité alimentaire avant la catastrophe.

lemonde.title: Le maintien du brevet en dépit de la canicule suscite la colère des équipes éducatives : « L’épreuve a bien eu lieu, mais dans de mauvaises conditions »
lemonde.description: Quelque 850 000 élèves de troisième, déjà épuisés par une semaine de chaleur, ont passé, vendredi, l’épreuve de français dans des classes où il pouvait faire jusqu’à 35 °C, au risque de créer des ruptures d’égalité en fonction des établissements.

lemonde.title: Netflix, devenu un pilier de la création française, demande le « plafonnement » de ses investissements obligatoires
lemonde.description: La plateforme américaine alerte sur la « viabilité des règles actuelles de financement par les diffuseurs », qui lui demandent de consacrer 20 % de son chiffre d’affaires aux créations françaises et européennes. Netflix investit 250 millions d’euros par an en séries, documentaires et films français.

lemonde.title: Le Burkina Faso annonce rompre ses relations diplomatiques avec la France
lemonde.description: Le régime militaire d’Ouagadougou accuse Paris d’« activisme incessant » contre ses intérêts, après plusieurs années de fortes tensions entre les deux pays.

lemonde.title: Les médias chinois muets des heures après le crash d’un avion biplace contre la plus haute tour de Pékin
lemonde.description: L’appareil a percuté l’immeuble en pleine heure de pointe, pour des raisons encore inconnues. Strictement contrôlée par l’Etat, la presse ne s’en était pas fait l’écho vendredi, alors que les locaux de la télévision nationale se situent tout près de la tour.

lemonde.description: Le territoire, occupé par la Russie depuis 2014, a été placé en « situation d’urgence » au niveau régional par les autorités russes locales, pour faire face aux conséquences des récentes frappes ukrainiennes, qui ont causé des pénuries de carburant et d’électricité.

lemonde.title: En Tunisie, la militante des droits humains Sihem Bensedrine condamnée à 25 ans de prison
lemonde.description: L’ancienne journaliste est mise en cause pour son travail à la tête de l’Instance Vérité & Dignité, créée après la révolution de 2011. Sa condamnation intervient dans un contexte de durcissement de la répression des voix critiques en Tunisie.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : Gérald Darmanin a « perdu la confiance des magistrats », selon l’Union syndicale des magistrats, leur principal syndicat
lemonde.description: Le président du tribunal de Paris, Peimane Ghaleh-Marzban, a mis en garde les politiques contre des propositions « empreintes de simplicité et d’à à-peu-près ».

lemonde.description: Dans cette dystopie drôle et émouvante, l’écrivain américain évoque des Etats-Unis plus que jamais autoritaires à travers les yeux de Vera, une jeune surdouée.

lemonde.description: Cette annonce est concomitante de la décision du gendarme financier du football français, la DNCG, d’encadrer la masse salariale du club lyonnais la saison prochaine.

lemonde.description: Les autorités s’alarment de la consommation croissante de cette cathinone de synthèse, qui provoque une forte accoutumance et de graves risques pour la santé. La préfecture lance un plan de 60 actions, dévoilé vendredi, intitulé « Zéro drogue. La Réunion dit non ».

zeit.title: USA: Israel, Libanon und die USA unterzeichnen Rahmenabkommen
zeit.description: Ein Rahmenvertrag soll ein Friedensabkommen zwischen Israel und dem Libanon ermöglichen. Unterstützt von den USA gaben die beiden Länder eine Einigung bekannt.

zeit.title: Thomas Diener: Von einem, der über die Brandmauer sprang
zeit.description: Die CDU kämpft in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern mit niedrigen Umfragewerten. Nun will ein Abgeordneter die Partei verlassen und zur AfD wechseln. Warum tut er das?

zeit.title: Zentrum für Politische Schönheit: Tragisch, aber nicht komisch
zeit.description: Was darf Satire, was darf Kunst? Nach Hausdurchsuchungen beim Zentrum für Politische Schönheit stellt sich diese Frage mal wieder. Vielleicht stellen wir mal eine andere.

zeit.title: USA: Donald Trump droht Europa mit 100-Prozent-Zöllen
zeit.description: Angesichts europäischer Digitalsteuer-Pläne kündigt der US-Präsident neue Zölle an. Den Angaben nach würden diese Zölle bereits vereinbarte Zollabkommen ersetzen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: USA greifen Iran an +++ Iranische Medien melden Angriff im Süden Irans
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Deutscher Wetterdienst misst neue Höchsttemperatur +++ AKW Beznau wegen hoher Temperatur der Aare abgestellt
nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf Mensch und Umwelt? Hier finden Sie die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Schwere Erdbeben erschüttern Venezuela: Zahl der Toten steigt auf 920 +++ Staatsfernsehen zeigt Ankunft von Rettungskräften aus der Schweiz und Deutschland
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten richteten zwei Erdbeben in Venezuela verheerende Schäden an. Rettungskräfte suchen unter den Trümmern nach Überlebenden. Über das Ausmass der Schäden ist wenig bekannt.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Handelsstreit: Trump droht Europäern mit neuen Zöllen
nzz.description: Im Februar hat der Supreme Court Trumps Zölle für unrechtmässig erklärt. Doch der amerikanische Präsident verursacht mit seinen umstrittenen Zöllen weiter weltweit Turbulenzen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Hunderttausend Stellen werden gestrichen: Die Krise bei VW ist ein Menetekel für den Standort Deutschland
nzz.description: Jahrelang haben die EU und die Bundesregierung eine Politik gegen die Autoindustrie betrieben. Jetzt droht der Branche der Niedergang – und Deutschland der Verlust von Wohlstand. Das Land braucht eine 180-Grad-Wende in der Wirtschafts- und Energiepolitik.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Gluthitze dauert noch bis Sonntag – die besten Bilder
nzz.description: In Basel wurde heute Nachmittag mit 38,8 Grad Celsius der Hitzerekord von 2003 geknackt. In Saarbrücken (D) stieg das Thermometer gar auf 41,3 Grad. So heiss war es in Deutschland noch nie!

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Rechtsruck in Lateinamerika: Der Kampf gegen die Kriminalität hat oberste Priorität
nzz.description: Die Region vollzieht einen politischen Wandel. Fürs Erste hat der Sozialismus ausgedient. Die Menschen wollen Sicherheit, Ordnung und wirtschaftliches Wachstum.

nzz.title: Präsidentenanwärter und Leopardenretter: Putins langjähriger Weggefährte Sergei Iwanow ist gestorben
nzz.description: Der einstige KGB-Agent im Westen war mehr als zwei Jahrzehnte lang ein prägendes Gesicht im Umfeld des Kremlchefs. Am Schluss fand er als Naturschützer seine eigentliche Berufung.

nzz.title: Volkswagen könnte bis zu 100 000 Stellen abbauen und vier Werke schliessen
nzz.description: Ein Konzept der Konzernführung sieht beispiellose Einschnitte vor: In der Folge würde sich der deutsche Autobauer aus weiten Teilen Deutschlands verabschieden. Der Widerstand ist gross.

nzz.title: Das jüngste Opfer von Hegseths Umbau: Der Befehlshaber der US-Armee in Europa räumt seinen Posten
nzz.description: Chris Donahue sei «wie ein Actionheld aus einem Comic», sagte einst der Nato-Oberbefehlshaber. Er verliess als letzter amerikanischer Soldat Afghanistan – und wird nun auch aus Europa abgezogen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Feuerwerksinitiative kommt zur Abstimmung
Die Genfer Regierung hat ihre Ziele für den G-7-Gipfel erreicht. Doch ein Polizeieinsatz sorgt für Kritik
nzz.description: Der Staatsrat zieht eine positive Bilanz seines Sicherheitsdispositivs während des G-7-Gipfels im französischen Évian-les-Bains. Es bleiben jedoch Fragen offen.

nzz.title: Grossanlässe trotz Hitze: So funktioniert ein Triathlon bei 36 Grad
nzz.description: Für das Wochenende werden rekordverdächtig hohe Temperaturen vorausgesagt. Trotzdem finden in Zürich grosse Sportanlässe statt. Die Spitäler treffen Vorkehrungen.

nzz.title: Wer fährt an den Nato-Gipfel? In Tschechien tragen Staatspräsident Pavel und Regierungschef Babis einen Machtkampf um die Aussenpolitik aus
nzz.description: Die Regierung Babis wollte verhindern, dass der Staatspräsident Pavel nach Ankara reist. Dieser vermutet einen Racheakt – und erwirkte beim Verfassungsgericht seine Teilnahme am Nato-Gipfel.

nzz.title: Grosse Überwachung von kleinen Insekten: wie sich das Tessin gegen die Tigermücke wehrt
nzz.description: Invasive Insekten wie die Tigermücke breiten sich aus. Mit einem neuen Überwachungsprogramm rüsten sich Bund und Kantone gegen die Einschleppung tropischer Erreger.

nzz.title: An der WM rudern die Norweger und präsentieren sich als Wikinger – doch dieses Bild provoziert
nzz.description: Norwegen spielt erstmals seit 1998 an einer WM und zieht in den Sechzehntelfinal ein. Bei Toren der Nationalmannschaft schlagen bisweilen sogar Seismometer aus.

observador.title: Moradores em manifestação contra sala de consumo no Aleixo
observador.description: Dezenas de pessoas protestaram contra a transferência da sala de consumo assistido para o Aleixo. "Não é justo que esta zona seja massacrada outra vez com isto", critica morador.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Praia de Santo Amaro de Oeiras reaberta após forte poluição
observador.description: A interdição, imposta após uma descarga de lixiviados tratados na ribeira da Laje, foi levantada pela delegada de saúde. A Tratolixo nega responsabilidade.

observador.title: Julgamento de "Man Genas" suspenso até julho
observador.description: Influenciador angolano acusado de associação criminosa e ultraje ao Estado. Defesa alega absolvição prévia pelo Tribunal da Relação. Novo julgamento a 17 de julho.

observador.title: Lei Prestianni ainda é falada e um português em destaque
observador.description: Pedro Henriques diz que a "Lei Prestianni" tem sido bem utilizada no Mundial apesar das criticas. Destaca ainda a prestação da arbitragem portuguesa no Mundial com um nome em destaque: João Pinheiro.

observador.title: Neuville lidera Rali da Acrópole após sete classificativas
observador.description: Belga da Hyundai assumiu o comando logo na primeira especial da sexta-feira e terminou o dia com vantagem sobre Ogier e Fourmaux. Armstrong abandonou.

observador.title: TAP conclui emissão de dívida de 350 milhões de euros
observador.description: As obrigações seniores, com vencimento em 2031, foram emitidas com o menor spread de crédito de sempre da companhia, numa operação sobresubscrita por investidores.

observador.title: Seguro: futebol é "grande embaixador" de Portugal
observador.description: O Presidente da República discursou na abertura do Portugal Football Summit em Miami, onde Portugal defronta a Colômbia no sábado para o Mundial2026.

observador.title: De n.º 2 para 3. Rui Tavares é o mestre da ilusão política?
observador.description: Rui Tavares inventou a "despromoção para cima". Deixa de ser porta-voz para controlar "apenas" o conteúdo e a forma, para garantir que nada muda enquanto tudo parece mudar. O partido vai sobreviver?

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: O acordo da PSU é prenuncio de tranquilidade para o Governo?
observador.description: Numa semana, o executivo viu chumbada a reforma laboral e aprovada a PSU. Poderá estar aqui um raio de esperança para o Governo antes do Orçamento?

observador.title: OpenAI apresenta novas versões de IA e começa por parceiros
observador.description: A OpenAI revelou os planos a pedido de Washington, limitando o acesso inicial a "um pequeno grupo de parceiros de confiança". Lançamento amplo previsto para breve.

observador.title: Bruno, as raízes no Norte e a descendência dos Faria Salgado
observador.description: Bruno Fernandes nasceu em Gueifães e tem os antepassados próximos entre Porto e Braga. Mas como se explica o aventureirismo que o fez mudar para Itália antes dos 18? A família Faria Salgado dá pistas.

observador.title: Homem que esfaqueou mulher em Leiria fica em preventiva
observador.description: Após ter sido presente ao juiz de instrução criminal no Tribunal Judicial de Leiria foi-lhe aplicada a medida de coação de prisão preventiva, destaca a mesma fonte.

observador.title: Kiev angaria 10 mil milhões de euros para reconstrução
observador.description: A Conferência para a Reconstrução da Ucrânia terminou esta sexta-feira com cerca de 200 acordos assinados, incluindo 3,4 mil milhões de dólares do Banco Mundial.

observador.title: Comunidade lusa mobiliza-se após sismos na Venezuela
observador.description: Santuário de Fátima em Carrizal, centros portugueses e empresas como o Banco Plaza e supermercados Gama recolhem alimentos, roupa e medicamentos para as vítimas.

observador.title: Venezuela: Governo diz que Portugal pode enviar outro avião
observador.description: Luís Neves diz que Madeira e Açores querem enviar meios, mas articulação com Caracas é essencial. Primeiros KC-390 levam 64 elementos.

observador.title: Exclusão dos Açores de apoios agrícolas com impacto
observador.description: Em resposta a um requerimento do Chega nos Açores na Assembleia Regional, o executivo açoriano garante ter realizado diligências junto do Governo da República.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Sénégal déroule contre l'Irak et espère voir les 16es de finale
Mondial 2026 : le Sénégal déroule contre l'Irak et espère voir les 16es de finale
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal a largement battu l'Irak pour conclure sa phase de groupe de la Coupe du monde. Avec cette troisième place du groupe I, les Lions de la Teranga devront attendre la fin des autres groupes pour savoir s'ils passent en 16es de finale.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la France s'offre la Norvège et la première place du groupe I
Mondial 2026 : la France s'offre la Norvège et la première place du groupe I
france24fr.description: La France a facilement battu une Norvège largement remaniée pour s'adjuger la tête du groupe I de la Coupe du monde (4-1). Ousmane Dembélé a marqué un triplé, rejoignant ainsi un cercle fermé composé de Just Fontaine, Mbappé et lui-même.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : à Yaoundé, des milliers de ménages luttent pour avoir de l’eau potable
france24fr.description: Au Cameroun, l'accès à l'eau potable demeure un véritable défi pour des milliers de familles. Dans les grandes villes, la demande dépasse largement les capacités d'approvisionnement de la Société en charge. Reportage sur le quotidien de quelques ménages confrontés à la pénurie d'eau à Yaoundé.

france24fr.title: Littérature africaine : Réassi Ouabanzi veut créer des ponts entre l'Afrique et ses diasporas
france24fr.description: Comment donner plus de visibilité aux littératures africaines et afrodescendantes ? Nous revenons avec lui sur les nouveaux visages de

france24fr.title: Donald Trump menace l'UE sur les taxes numériques, Bruxelles contre-attaque
france24fr.description: Alors que Donald Trump a menacé, vendredi, de frapper de droits de douane de 100 % les pays européens qui mettraient en place une taxation des services numériques, l'Union européenne a assuré en réponse qu'elle réagirait "rapidement et avec détermination".

france24fr.title: Au Venezuela, au moins 920 morts après le double séisme
france24fr.description: Les secouristes s'activaient, vendredi, au Venezuela pour retrouver les survivants du double séisme qui a fait au moins 920 morts, selon les autorités, et quelque 50 000 disparus.

france24fr.title: Israël et le Liban ont signé un accord-cadre pour "une paix et une sécurité durables", annoncent les États-Unis
Israël, le Liban et les États-Unis concluent un accord-cadre
france24fr.description: Israël, le Liban et les États-Unis ont signé un accord-cadre vendredi à Washington, sans en dévoiler le contenu mais avec pour objectif affiché d'ouvrir la voie à "une paix et une sécurité durables", selon le secrétaire d'État américain Marco Rubio.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Les supporters sénégalais font les calculs avant d’affronter l’Irak
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Mondial 2026 : le Sénégal doit impérativement battre l'Irak pour espérer poursuivre son aventure. Après deux défaites lors de leurs deux premiers matchs, les Lions de la Teranga n'ont plus leur destin entièrement entre leurs mains. Les supporters sénégalais font déjà les calculs et espèrent un scénario favorable.

france24fr.title: Sénégal - Irak en direct : les Lions de la Teranga déroulent et espèrent
france24fr.description: Après des défaites contre la France et la Norvège, le Sénégal et l'Irak s'affrontent dans un match couperet, vendredi, pour décrocher la troisième place du groupe I, synonyme d'espoir pour une qualification pour les seizièmes de finale du Mondial. Suivez le match en direct sur france24.com grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: Guinée : l'opposant Rafiou Sow inculpé à Conakry, accusé de meurtre présumé au Canada en 2007
france24fr.description: En Guinée, l'opposant Rafiou Sow a été inculpé ce mercredi et placé sous mandat de dépôt, accusé du meurtre présumé de son épouse, survenue en 2007 au Canada. Une affaire qui secoue tout le pays.

france24fr.title: Renvoyé en procès pour viol, le footballeur Achraf Hakimi se pourvoit en cassation
france24fr.description: Le footballeur Achraf Hakimi, défenseur du PSG et capitaine de l'équipe nationale du Maroc, dont le renvoi en procès pour viol a été confirmé le 19 juin par la justice, se pourvoit en cassation, a indiqué vendredi à l'AFP une source proche du dossier.

france24fr.title: France - Norvège en direct : Dembélé en mode triplé, suivez la finale du groupe I du Mondial
france24fr.description: La France de Kylian Mbappé affronte la Norvège d'Erling Haaland vendredi à Boston dans un duel pour la 1re place du groupe I de la Coupe du monde. Qui des Bleus ou de Lansdlaget l'emportera ? Suivez le match en direct sur france24.com grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: Le Hezbollah se vante de détruire des batteries anti aériennes israéliennes… qui sont des leurres
france24fr.description: Le Hezbollah a récemment fait la promotion de vidéos censées montrer l’efficacité de sa nouvelle flotte de drones FPV, des engins quadricoptères équipés d’explosifs légers. Les images les montrent fonçant sur des batteries anti-missile israéliennes… qui s’avèrent être des leurres, mis en place justement pour tromper ces drones.

france24fr.title: Le pari d’une route alternative dans le détroit d’Ormuz
france24fr.description: Alors qu'emprunter la route maritime longeant les côtes omanaises est souvent présentée comme une voie de contournement face au risque de mines dans le détroit d'Ormuz, cette stratégie est remise en question après l'attaque d'un cargo jeudi. Cet épisode illustre la complexité de la navigation dans ce passage, au cœur du bras de fer entre Téhéran et Washington.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : des chefs réinventent la gastronomie traditionnelle
france24fr.description: Dans la capitale Kinshasa, une nouvelle génération de chefs s'approprie les recettes traditionnelles de la République démocratique du Congo. Dans ce pays de plus de 110 millions d’habitants, la haute gastronomie peine encore à émerger.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 live: Norwegen gegen Frankreich – Norwegen verschießt Elfmeter
spiegel.description: Ousmane Dembélé überragt im Gruppenfinale zwischen Norwegen und Frankreich. Die Norweger vergeben große Chancen. Die Erkenntnisse zum Spiel.

spiegel.title: USA-Iran-Krieg: USA greifen laut Armee Ziele in Iran an
spiegel.description: Das US-Militär hat nach eigenen Angaben Angriffe gegen Iran durchgeführt, trotz vereinbarter Waffenruhe. Die Luftschläge waren demnach gegen Raketen- und Drohnenlager sowie Radaranlagen an der Küste gerichtet.

spiegel.title: Isernhagen in Niedersachsen: Achtjähriger stirbt nach Unglück in Badesee
spiegel.description: Zwei Stunden suchten Rettungskräfte und Freiwillige in Isernhagen bei Hannover nach einem Kind, das im Parksee Lohne gebadet hatte und dort untergegangen war.

spiegel.title: Manuel Neuer: »Alle keine Ahnung!« Timo Hildebrand geht auf Neuer-Kritiker los
spiegel.description: Manuel Neuer machte bei der Niederlage gegen Ecuador keine gute Figur. Aber trug er auch eine Schuld? Sein Vorgänger Timo Hildebrand hat dazu eine klare Meinung.

spiegel.title: Israel und Libanon einigen sich auf Rahmenabkommen
spiegel.description: Noch am Donnerstagabend gab es israelische Angriffe im Südlibanon. Jetzt haben die Botschafter beider Länder in Washington eine Vereinbarung unterzeichnet.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Präsident droht im Fall einer Digitalsteuer mit 100-Prozent-Zöllen
spiegel.description: US-Präsident Trump versucht, die Daumenschrauben anzusetzen: Er stellt allen Ländern, die eine Digitalsteuer gegen amerikanische Konzerne planen, drastische Konsequenzen in Aussicht. Die EU reagiert.

spiegel.title: Fall Fabian aus Güstrow: Was Tatbild und Tatort über Täter oder Täterin verraten
spiegel.description: Fallanalytiker haben die Tötung des achtjährigen Fabian aus Güstrow rekonstruiert. Vor Gericht berichtet ein Profiler des LKA Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, was Tatbild und Tatort über den Mörder verraten. Oder die Mörderin.

spiegel.title: Erdbeben in Venezuela: UN melden mehr als 50.000 Vermisste
spiegel.description: Erste internationale Suchtrupps, auch aus Deutschland, erreichen nach dem Erdbeben Venezuela. Die Zahl der Toten hat sich auf 920 erhöht, dürfte aber noch weiter steigen.

spiegel.title: Schwergewichts-Champion Oleksandr Ussyk legt WM-Titel nieder
spiegel.description: Machtwechsel im Schwergewichtsboxen: Oleksandr Ussyk gibt seine drei WM-Gürtel kampflos auf. Sein deutscher Herausforderer Agit Kabayel könnte nun zum Champion aufsteigen, ohne dafür in den Ring zu müssen.

spiegel.title: Deutschland bei der WM 2026: Was die Daten über die DFB-Elf verraten
spiegel.description: Bei der WM liefert die Fifa zu jedem Spiel zahlreiche Statistiken. Sie zeigen, wer besonders hart arbeitet. Wie schwer der Ausfall von Nico Schlotterbeck wiegt. Und was der deutschen Elf gegen Ecuador wirklich fehlte.

spiegel.title: USA: So kapern extreme Minderheiten die Politik
spiegel.description: Die USA, das Land der politischen Extreme? Stimmt nicht, zeigt eine neue Studie. Zwar gibt es lautstarke Gruppen an den Rändern, aber viele Amerikaner vertreten ziemlich moderate Positionen. Was das für anstehende Wahlen bedeutet.

spiegel.title: USA-Iran-Krieg: Donald Trump wirft Iran Bruch der Waffenruhe in der Straße von Hormus vor
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident spricht von einem »törichten Verstoß gegen unsere Vereinbarung«: Donald Trump wirft Iran vor, mehrere Drohnenangriffe auf Schiffe in der Straße von Hormus durchgeführt zu haben, konkretisiert seine Vorwürfe allerdings nicht.

spiegel.title: Best of Samira El Ouassil: Das ist meine letzte Kolumne. Und trotzdem nicht die traurigste
spiegel.description: Knapp 290 Kolumnen habe ich in sechs Jahren für den SPIEGEL geschrieben. Zum Abschied verrate ich Ihnen, welche am besten gealtert ist. Und welche am schlechtesten.

spiegel.title: Hitze in Europa: 100 Grad Bodentemperatur auf der Baustelle – und Schneematsch am Mont Blanc
spiegel.description: Bei über 40 Grad fallen Großevents aus, Geschäfte schließen früher. Und was die Menschen in Rom zu spüren bekommen, macht Greenpeace mit Kameras sichtbar.

spiegel.title: Hitzewelle in Deutschland: Klimakrise steht nicht auf dem Totenschein
spiegel.description: Der Notarzt Jörg Schmid erlebt derzeit, wie Menschen in überhitzten Wohnungen sterben. Er sagt: Sie sind Opfer der Klimakrise.

spiegel.title: Hitze: 41,3 Grad – Wetterdienst meldet deutschlandweiten Hitzerekord
spiegel.description: Erstmals seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen wurden in Deutschland 41,3 Grad gemessen. Auch mehrere Bundesländer brechen Rekorde. Und: Großveranstaltungen werden in ganz Europa abgesagt. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Der Ohnmächtige
spiegel.description: Die Attacken von Julian Nagelsmann gegen die Schiedsrichter im Spiel gegen Ecuador offenbaren ein größeres Problem: die grassierende Unfähigkeit, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, wenn etwas schiefgeht.

spiegel.title: John Bolton: Ehemaliger Berater von Donald Trump bekennt sich in Dokumentenaffäre schuldig
spiegel.description: John Bolton hat illegal Geheimdokumente aufbewahrt. Das hat der ehemalige Sicherheitsberater von Donald Trump nun vor Gericht gestanden. Zunächst hatte er auf nicht schuldig plädiert. Ihm droht eine Haftstrafe.

Columnist Karmela Padavic-Callaghan explores how these could change our understanding of quantum physics, or even help us make better devices

new-sci.description: IBM's latest chip packs in twice as many transistors as the current state-of-the-art chip by adding a second layer of silicon circuitry

new-sci.description: Phages, viruses that infect bacteria, could be genetically manipulated to destroy cancerous cells using the immunity we have acquired from vaccines

new-sci.description: Scrolls from the Roman library of Herculaneum that were carbonised by a volcanic eruption have been read in their entirety for the first time, thanks to scans and AI software

new-sci.description: Feedback isn't sure what to make of a ground-breaking piece of research into the understudied topic of "subjective individual variability in onion tearing and its relationship to chemosensory sensitivity"

new-sci.description: An instrument on the Perseverance rover has identified large, complex carbon compounds alongside unusual patterns on the surface of rocks that resemble traces of microbial activity

phys-org.title: Clean crystal surface lets single molecules hit ultimate quantum limit
phys-org.description: Scientists at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light (MPL) have developed a technique for interrogating molecules on surfaces with spectroscopic precision, thereby reaching the ultimate quantum limit for the first time. With their findings, published in Science, the researchers open new opportunities for the study of molecule-surface interactions and molecular quantum technologies.

phys-org.title: Ocean warming above 1.5°C triggered year-round marine disruption across globe, study shows
phys-org.description: Researchers at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) led one of the first global assessments of how marine ecosystems responded during the first year when global temperatures temporarily exceeded 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

phys-org.title: Japan's small cities may face higher care burdens under the compact city policy
phys-org.description: As populations decline and age across the developed world, compact city strategies, which oversee the consolidation of urban facilities and guide residents toward transit-served hubs, have become mainstream policies. Yet most evidence about their benefits comes from cities that are already compact. Far less is known about the social costs that may arise during the transition to compactness in the small and medium-sized cities (SMCs) most exposed to shrinkage.

phys-org.title: ROS-producing enzymes guide plant cell division and tissue patterning, gene-editing study shows
phys-org.description: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) produced naturally during cellular metabolism often cause oxidative damage to cells. However, these molecules also play an important role in normal cellular signaling. While ROS are established as essential signaling molecules in various organisms, their precise role in basic plant development and morphogenesis remains unclear.

phys-org.title: Pegasus launch to deploy LINK for months‑long orbit boost of aging Swift
phys-org.description: A mission to raise the orbit of NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is poised for launch no earlier than Tuesday, June 30, at 6:23 a.m. EDT (10:23 p.m. UTC+12), from Kwajalein Atoll, part of the Republic of the Marshall Islands in the South Pacific Ocean.

phys-org.title: Plasma and graphene combine to protect metal surfaces from corrosion
phys-org.description: Plasma is an ionized gas, often referred to as the fourth state of matter. Plasmas, which are created artificially by applying energy to a gas, are found in the fluorescent tubes that illuminate kitchens. However, they have many other possible applications, such as the production of graphene.

phys-org.title: Glass cells of atoms offer a new path to smarter, cheaper sensors
phys-org.description: More accurate navigation systems and improved wireless communications may not come from traditional electronics, but rather from atoms. Researchers at Penn State and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have developed a new way to build tinier, smarter glass sensors filled with highly precise and stable atoms.

phys-org.title: Hubble spies ancient 'Chandelier Cluster' forming stars in two bursts
phys-org.description: The subject of today's NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image is an ancient inhabitant of our galaxy. This sparkling scene features a globular cluster: a collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars, all tightly bound together under the influence of gravity. There are more than 150 globular clusters in our galaxy, though there may be others still undiscovered, hidden from view by dust or densely packed fields of stars.

phys-org.title: Beetle-like borings in 70-million-year-old titanosaur fossils reshape Lo Hueco fossil story

These perforations, known as bioerosion structures, provide information that helps us understand relationships between living organisms in the past, reconstruct palaeoecosystems and improve our understanding of the fossilization process. phys-org.title: NASA's PACE mission studies smoke and fires
phys-org.description: With the North American fire season underway, and a record number of acres already burned nationwide, NASA's Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, and ocean Ecosystem (PACE) satellite's three instruments are observing vegetation precursors to fires, along with plumes of smoke and their movement. These data will help scientists piece together clues that deepen their understanding of wildfires.

phys-org.title: Unknown 4,000-year-old stone circle in Belfast uncovered by archaeologists
phys-org.description: Archaeologists have uncovered an unknown stone circle that dates back at least 4,000 years to the Late Neolithic or Early Bronze Age and was most likely used for ritual activities.

phys-org.title: How atomic defects can program carbon quantum dots for future light-based technologies
phys-org.description: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are tiny carbon-based nanomaterials that have attracted increasing attention as environmentally friendly alternatives to conventional heavy-metal quantum dots. They are lightweight, photostable and potentially biocompatible, and their light absorption and emission properties can be tuned.

phys-org.title: Evidence identifies ancient Aboriginal mining in the Riverland
phys-org.description: Flinders University researchers, in partnership with the River Murray and Mallee Aboriginal Corporation, have found evidence that points to 7,000 years of Aboriginal mining of stone at Sugarloaf Hill in South Australia's Riverland. The dating formed part of the first detailed investigation into an Aboriginal chert and silcrete quarry in the Riverland region.

phys-org.title: Apple rootstock response varies to threshold water management during 6 weeks of progressing drought
phys-org.description: As drought and water uncertainty put increasing pressure on orchard systems, researchers at the USDA Agricultural Research Service's Appalachian Fruit Research Station in Kearneysville, West Virginia, launched a study in response to strong grower interest in how modern apple rootstocks hold up under drought stress. phys-org.title: Far-red radiation and elevated CO₂ boost biomass accumulation in young leaf lettuce indoors
phys-org.description: A new study from scientists at Purdue University reports that far-red radiation, in combination with increased carbon dioxide (CO₂) concentration, significantly enhances biomass production in young leaf lettuce grown under controlled environments, offering practical guidance for indoor farming operators enthusiastic about including far-red in their sole-source lighting recipes.

phys-org.title: Rising heat and humidity challenge energy-efficient data center cooling worldwide
phys-org.description: Reliable operation of data centers has become essential to nearly all sectors of modern society, including health care, education, government services, power grid operation, banking, defense and disaster relief. New research published in Scientific Reports, led by University of Hawai'i (UH) at Mānoa atmospheric scientists reveals that future climate conditions may reduce the availability of one of the cheapest and most energy-efficient approaches to cooling data centers.

phys-org.title: How coworkers shape careers: Learning and competition pull in opposite directions
phys-org.description: New research, published by the Rockwool Foundation Berlin (RFBerlin), shows that co-workers can have powerful—but opposing—effects on the careers of young workers. While some colleagues foster learning and long-term success, others may hinder career progression through direct competition. phys-org.title: May 2024 superstorm drew most ring current ions from Earth, not solar wind, research reveals
phys-org.description: In May 2024, auroras were observed at unusually low latitudes across the globe, lighting up skies that rarely see such displays. Inside Earth's magnetosphere, the region of space surrounding our planet and dominated by its intrinsic magnetic field, something significant was finally observed.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.
